findings: On the fixed FP32-storage matrix, FP16 and BF16 are effectively tied in warm eager time (~0.18s) and compiled time (~0.096s); strict FP32 is slower (~0.331s eager, ~0.266s compiled).
Compilation speeds up BF16/FP16 by approximately 1.88/1.89x versus fully eager in this small-batch forward/backward diagnostic. This is not a production end-to-end speedup.

FP16 compiled gradients are substantially closer to strict FP32 eager than BF16 compiled gradients: first-batch global relative L2 is 0.234% versus 1.732%; raw-BT4 gradient relative L2 is 0.545% versus 3.317%. All three batches are finite.

FP16 eager and compiled match FP32 eager teacher-forced root choices on all 192 diagnostic positions and native policy choices on the first 64. BF16 compiled disagrees on 2/192 teacher-forced roots and 1/64 native choices. These are small numerical diagnostics, not playing-strength measurements.

FP32 compiled matches FP32 eager closely, with all-batch global gradient cosine above 0.99999999. The previously reported large BT4 compilation discrepancy is not reproduced under this different checkpoint/input/storage/runtime protocol. Its historical cause remains unisolated.
Compilation improves the global-gradient error relative to FP32 for both low-precision formats, but not every tensor or discrete move; do not equate eager agreement with accuracy.
Cold first forward/backward takes 75.95s FP32, 100.41s BF16 and 99.28s FP16; includes compilation, autotuning and first-use overhead. Narrower arithmetic did not shorten cold start here.

timing_sensitivity.interpretation: Production control has one 0.395s repeat versus ~0.118s median, inflating its 0.147s mean; report both and do not advertise the mean-only ~1.53x ratio as a robust production gain. Median comparison is ~1.23x speed (~19% less time). No repeats discarded; no production batch or optimizer timing yet.

precision_scope.matrix_parameter_and_gradient_storage: FP32, checkpoint values promoted exactly; existing BF16 weight quantization cannot be undone
precision_scope.fp16_compute: FP16 with existing FP32 normalization/statistics/loss islands and fixed loss scaling 128; finite over three batches is not a long-training stability guarantee
precision_scope.production_control: Original mixed FP32/BF16 parameter storage, eager BT4, compiled fresh regions, high/TF32 and native reduction settings. Different storage/settings from the controlled matrix.

next_step_not_launched: Test the promising compiled FP16/FP32-storage runtime against the exact production configuration at batch 1024, including data, optimizer and checkpoint-resume behavior; explicitly distinguish FP32 optimizer/master-state changes from a runtime-only optimization. Then bounded multi-update stability and common-pool validation before long training or play claims. No training runtime was switched.
